html:
Pilsner is a pale, clear lager first brewed in the Bohemian town of Plzeň, in German Pilsen, by the Bavarian brewer Josef Groll, who served the first batch on 5 October 1842.

The town's citizens had founded a new brewery after their beer turned so bad that barrels were poured out in public. Groll combined soft local water, pale malt dried with indirect heat, Saaz hops and Bavarian bottom fermenting yeast, kept cold in sandstone cellars. The result was golden and clear, which suited the new cheap glassware. Railways spread it across Europe, and the brewery registered Pilsner Urquell, the original source, in 1898. Most beer drunk in the world today is a pale lager descended from it. Czechs drink more beer per person than any other nation. It drew on the Bavarian beer tradition, and Plzeň was also home to the Škoda Works.
sum: Pilsner is a pale, clear lager first brewed in the Bohemian town of Plzeň, in German Pilsen, by the Bavarian brewer Josef Groll, who served the first batch on 5 October 1842.
